items.briefing:
Scammers are targeting Microsoft Teams users with voice phishing ("vishing") attacks, where they impersonate trusted contacts to trick people into handing over credentials or sensitive information. If your organisation uses Teams, staff should be cautious about unexpected calls or requests — even from what appears to be a known contact. Separately, a serious security flaw has been discovered in SonicWall SMA 1000 devices that could allow attackers to break in without needing a password. If your organisation uses this equipment, check with your IT team about applying patches urgently.

**Practical tip:** If you receive an unexpected Teams call asking for login details or urgent action, hang up and verify the request through a separate, known contact method before doing anything.

featured.title: AI’s Vulnerability Surge May Be More Manageable Than First Feared
featured.summary: New research suggests the coming Vulnpocalypse may not be so overwhelming for enterprise security teams — if they have the right strategies.
